page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Native family, built on KVM virtualization. The instance provisions 20 shared vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 64.0 GB of RAM. This provides approximately 3.2 GB of memory per core. The underlying x86_64 architecture features 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache. Hardware cryptographic flags including AES and SHA-NI are active, along with standard AVX, BMI2, and FMA instructions, though newer extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are not supported. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a balance skewed toward general parallel execution rather than heavy raw computational density. Geekbench testing reports strong results with a single-core score of 2055.0 and a multi-core score of 16287.0, supported by strong text processing capabilities. Conversely, synthetic stress-ng single-core performance scores in the lower tier at 784.29, reflecting the baseline 2.0 GHz clock and shared CPU model, while multi-core output scales reliably into the mid-range with a score of 15708.05. Memory operations align with expected multi-channel DDR4 bandwidth metrics, measuring 69.81 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 29.73 GB/sec for writes.

Operational throughput tests show consistent mid-tier behavior across application-level tasks. Redis workloads achieve 27.79 million SET operations per second, static web serving reaches 10.65 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations register at 11316.86. Small-scale CPU-based LLM inference achieves 260.19 tokens per second on 135M models and 18.03 tokens per second on 7B models, though large 70B parameter text generation is impractical without accelerator support.

The absence of included local storage and public IPv4 addresses necessitates external block storage volumes and network provisioning. The shared CPU profile presents a cost-effective alternative for horizontal multi-threaded services that do not require dedicated core isolation. UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is best suited for horizontally scaled web services, microservice clusters, container scheduling nodes, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier in-memory caching systems.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 20 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance delivers a 3.2 GB per-core memory ratio with hardware acceleration for standard AVX and AES instructions. Benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-range multi-core efficiency, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 16287.0 and 27.79 million Redis SET operations per second, counterbalanced by modest single-thread synthetic results due to the shared core model. The server includes no bundled local disk storage or GPU resources, requiring network storage attachments. The configuration offers cost-efficient compute and memory scale for multi-threaded workloads, making it well fitted for containerized application hosting, CI/CD runners, web serving pools, and caching layers.
